why: B47 (owner decision 2026-09-16, ADR-0154 accepted with option 'continuous'): the owner's
Windows device listens continuously, without the browser. Two halves meet here. The
Session Companion decides what the microphone may send and reports what it is doing; the
Cloud Core reads that report from the heartbeat and reconciles an alarm the device
snoozed on its own while the cloud was unreachable.
Every number and name below is one both halves would otherwise restate: the pre-roll
bound that makes 'raw audio is never kept' checkable, the indicator states the owner sees
and the cloud reports, the offline command set and WHEN each may act, and the shape of a
local snooze. That restating is this repository's most repeated bug shape, and the reason
packages/protocol/ exists.
The microphone is opened by the owner-session companion only; the Session-0 service
never loads a capture type. Audio that the local voice-activity detector did not admit
is kept in a bounded in-memory ring (at most max_preroll_ms) and zeroed when it falls
out; nothing is ever written to disk or logged. max_segment_ms bounds what the local
keyword spotter holds for one utterance. Listening can be turned OFF from anywhere and
ON only at the device: a cloud that could open the owner's microphone would be the one
surface this design exists not to have.
The compact health of the device voice service, attached to every heartbeat through the
same companion status object as the alarm fields (DEVICE_PROTOCOL.md 6g). Only states,
flags, a counter and an error CLASS: never a transcript, a phrase, a device name or audio.
Small and safe on purpose: each command stops, defers or reports something, and none
reaches a file, an account or another machine. 'offline_only' commands act locally only
while the Cloud Core is unreachable; while it is reachable the same words travel the
normal voice path and the cloud acts, so one sentence never acts twice. 'always' is
reserved for turning listening OFF, which is idempotent and only ever takes away.
The engine matches the owner's own enrolled recordings. It is a keyword matcher, never
an identity check: nothing here may authorise anything.
B13 requirement 259's local trigger. The device can only snooze an alarm it was told how
to snooze: the arm and the ring carry snooze_minutes and snoozes_left from the alarm row,
so the device never keeps its own default or its own limit. It reports WHEN it will ring
again ('until'), and the cloud adopts that instant rather than re-deriving it from the
moment the report arrived - one clock for one decision.
